title: Databases
note: A relational database stores rows in tables linked by keys and is queried with SQL. A transaction groups statements so they succeed or fail together, with the ACID guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability. Indexes speed up reads at the cost of extra storage and slower writes.

read.title: Transactions keep data honest
text: Moving money between accounts takes two updates: subtract from one, add to the other. If the program crashes between them, money vanishes. A transaction prevents that by grouping statements into one unit. Atomicity means all of it happens or none does. Consistency means each commit leaves constraints such as foreign keys satisfied. Durability means a committed change survives a crash, usually because it was written to a log first.

Isolation is the subtle letter. Perfect isolation, called Serializable, makes concurrent transactions behave as if they ran one after another, but it costs throughput. Weaker levels allow specific anomalies. Read Committed blocks dirty reads of uncommitted data but lets a row change between two reads. Repeatable Read keeps rows stable but, in the SQL standard, still allows phantom rows to appear in a repeated range query.

Distributed databases face a harder limit. Eric Brewer's CAP theorem says that when a network partition splits the nodes, a system must either refuse some requests to stay consistent or keep answering and risk returning stale data. Many NoSQL systems choose availability and settle for eventual consistency, where replicas agree once the partition heals.
